questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

My pocket has been picked.

options.text: Someone’s pocket has been picked by me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Someone has picked my pocket."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **subject** of the provided sentence is clearly being "**acted upon**" (or is in the** passive form**), so, we have to **apply verbs** **according** to the **passive **voice.
 
• Apparently, the sentence is in **present perfect tense** form as the event that is being talked about has already started in the past and is having an effect on the present **(has + been)**, so we will use the following structure:
 
• Active Voice : **Subject + has/have+ v3+ object**
 
• Passive Voice: **Object+ has/have+ been+ V3+ by + subject**
 
 
• Example: *Nikita has challenged Leena. (**Active**)*
 
• Example:* Leena has been challenged by Nikita. (**Passive**)*
 
 
 
• Thus, the active voice of "My pocket has been **picked**" is "Someone **has** picked my pocket".
 
• Hence, the active voice is: *Someone has picked my pocket.​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let us take a look at the remaining sentences:

 
• Someone’s pocket has been picked by me - This is **not **an **active voice** form as (**by**) is applied here.
 
• Someone had my pocket picked - This is in the **past perfect tense** **(had**) and we require present perfect tense (has) so this sentence is also **incorrect**.
 
• I picked someone’s pocket - This sentence is in the **simple past tense** (**picked**) and we need present perfect tense (has) so this sentence is also **not** **appropriate**.

• **Sentence c**, that is, 'He detested tyranny and institutionalized servitude' is **continuing** the **story** of PB Shelly and telling us how he hated tyranny. That is why this will be the third sentence.

The movie I watched last Saturday was __much better interesting__ than the one I watched today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**much more interesting**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence needs improvement.
 
• We can't say "more better" because "**better**" is the **comparative** version of "**good**". So we may now say "**much better**." In order to convey that something is **desirable**, we can say "much better."
 
• Additionally, "**much**" is used to** describe** a lot or a** bunch** of anything. The** comparative** degree of "**much** or many" is the word "**more**." It denotes "a larger quantity" of something.
 
• In the above-mentioned sentence, "**movie**" is the **noun** and "**interesting**" is **modifying** "**movie**". So, if we will put "better" with "interesting" then the sentence will become **redundant **and ultimately incorrect.
 
• Thus, we will apply "**much more interesting**" in the sentence to improve it.
 
• The complete sentence is: *The movie I watched last Saturday was much more interesting__ than the one I watched today.**​*​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Positive**, **comparative**, and **superlative **degrees of comparison are the several categories for degrees of comparison.

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has the highest Scheduled Tribe population (14.7 per cent).
 
• **Madhya Pradesh **is one of the **most populated states in India and has the highest tribal population in the country touching a galloping number of 15.31 million and covering 21.1% of the state's population.**
 
• Spread across **705 tribes**, they account for** ****8.6% of the country's total population. **
 
• There are **46** **recognized Scheduled Tribes in Madhya Pradesh**, India, three of which have been identified as '**Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PTGs)(formerly known as 'Special Primitive Tribal Groups').**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are **thirty-one** **(31) notified Scheduled Tribes in the state Gujrat**, which are as follows:** 1 Kharadi. 2 Balat. 4 Bhil, Bhil Taviyad, Bhil Garasia, Dholi Bhil, Dungri Bhil, Dungri Garasia, Mewasi Bhil, Malivad bhil, Rawal Bhil, Tadvi Bhil, Bhagalia, Bhilala, Pawra, Valvi, Vasava, Vasave, Katara, Bhabhor.**
 
• The tribes of** Jharkhand consist of** **32** tribes inhabiting the Jharkhand state in India. 
 
• **Gond tribes** have the largest population in **Chhattisgarh.**
